# Task 12 Stage 1, resubmission for Gate A round 3 (2026-11-20c)

**Status: Stage 1 output after Gate A rounds 1 and 2 failed; before Gate A round 3.** Generated by `python -m conceptual.report` from `runs/task12/stage1/2026-11-20c` (commit `d162aeabbd`, ledger sha256 `cfd459c04487`, engines sha256 `b4183d2504eb`). Every number is read from those files. Methods: Raymer, *Aircraft Design: A Conceptual Approach*, 2nd ed. (1992), through `conceptual/`. Review records: `docs/reviews/2026-11-20_task12_gateA_round1.md` and `..._round2.md`.

## Summary

- **Scoring favours the pusher** with the round-1 criteria and weights (4.13 against 3.95; only W0 is computed, the rest are judgement grades). Éder froze the pusher at round 1 and switched to the tractor at round 2 on figures a sign error had distorted, so the concept is asked again at round 3. Both designs are kept and reported.
- **Pusher with the PBS_TP100**: take-off weight **2,538 lb** (1,151 kg), empty 1,365 lb, fuel 673 lb, payload 500 lb; W/S 18 lb/ft^2, A 10, span 37.5 ft (11.4 m). The tractor with the same engine: 2,316 lb.
- **The engine sets the weight.** With a rubber engine the same aircraft would be 1,890 lb (159 shp). The PBS_TP100 gives 241 shp against 208 needed (ceiling binds). Split of the +647 lb: the larger engine itself (weight, and through its higher top speed the design q and gust loads) +168 lb, measured with Raymer's Table 3.4 consumption; its datasheet consumption (0.901 lb/(hp h) against 0.5 and 0.6) +480 lb. The engine figures are search extracts of the maker's pages and must be checked against the datasheet (engines.yaml).
- Requirements: 17 checked rows met, 2 not met: R9 negative gust within the negative limit; main gear stows (overturn 63 deg sets the track, p. 232).
- Empty weight: build-up 0.538 of W0, Table 3.1 x 0.95 0.547 (decomposition in section 4).
- First pass (Table 3.1 with sketch values) 2,110 lb. Method tests: `84 passed in 0.38s`.

## 0. What changed after Gate A round 1

| Finding or ruling | Change |
|---|---|
| F1 main gear missing from the balance | Main gear placed by the 15 deg tipback rule (p. 232) and included in the CG; nose-wheel load and propeller clearance checked |
| F2 gust at take-off weight only | Gust at take-off and zero-fuel weight, sea level and mission altitude; the largest sets the limit load |
| F3 q inconsistent with the V-n | Weight equations use q at the design cruise speed V_C (sea-level maximum level speed) |
| F4 crew-item explanation | Decomposition reported (section 4) |
| F5 ceiling grid artefact | Ceiling by bisection with CD0 at altitude; the last passing altitude is reported |
| F6 hard-coded speed text | The mission records which legs the 1.3 V_stall floor set; the text is generated from it |
| F7 constraint diagram | Landing limit searched to 200 lb/ft^2; best-range and best-loiter W/S and the R16 turn added |
| F8 test coverage | Tests for methods without printed values (identities, limits, Table 10.4 against Mattingly's PT6A-42); equation-to-test table (section 10) |
| F9 constants in the code | Moved to the ledger with sources and bands (appendix A) |
| F10 calibration list, polar, propeller | Section 9; drag polar and propeller operating points added |
| F11 trim and rotation | Trim on every mission leg at its fuel state; nose rotation at 0.8 V_TO with the forward CG (p. 432-433); tail enlarged where rotation needs it |
| Engine (Éder: find a small turboprop) | PBS TP100 (241 shp, 135.8 lb, 0.901 lb/(hp h)) fixed; Turbotech TP-R90, PT6A-42 and rubber compared |
| R9 negative limit (Éder: raise it) | Ledger -1.8 (GA utility); see section 7 |
| Round 2 N1 rotation sign | Main-wheel reaction and friction both nose-down; flap moment (16.17, Fig. 16.9) and wing moment (16.16) added; ground effect not modelled; sign test added |
| Round 2 N2 nose-load display | Limits shown as 5-20 % with the 8-15 % optimum; the nose wheel moves forward in its band when above the optimum |
| Round 2 N3 overturn and track | Half-track for the 63 deg overturn limit (p. 232) and a stowage check against the wing depth |
| Round 2 N4 pusher rotation angle | Pusher at 10 deg with a tail bumper (favourable end); tractor clearance with the nose strut compressed |
| Round 2 N6 engine attribution | Split into engine size and consumption with a Table 3.4 run of the same engine |
| Round 2 scoring | Round-1 weights restored; layout limits applied as constraints, not scored rows |
| Round 2 F9 tyre drag | Regular wheel and tyre 0.25 (Table 12.5 p. 287) instead of the faired 0.13 |

Scoring: the round-1 criteria and weights, unchanged; only W0 is computed. The pusher is evaluated at the favourable end of the rotation band: a tail bumper limits rotation to 10 deg, which still needs a 59 in main gear for 9 in of propeller clearance (p. 222, 232). The tall gear raises the CG, so the tipback rule moves the wheels aft and loads the nose wheel; the nose wheel is then moved forward inside its band. Rotation (corrected for the round-2 sign error) sizes the horizontal tail of both concepts. A raised thrust line is not modelled.

Empty-fraction decomposition (reviewer finding F4):

| Quantity | Fraction of W0 |
|---|---|
| component build-up with composite factors (this design) | 0.538 |
| same build-up without the Table 15.4 composite factors | 0.576 |
| crew items Raymer's GA set would add: furnishings (15.59); air conditioning (15.58) is zero with no crew | 0.033 |
| metal build-up plus crew items | 0.609 |
| Table 3.1 fit, general aviation single | 0.576 |
| Table 3.1 fit x 0.95 (composite) | 0.547 |
| Table 6.2 fit x 0.95 | 0.650 |
| Table 15.2 approximate group weights | 0.540 |

The build-up is 0.009 of W0 below the Table 3.1 fit x 0.95; the crew items alone are 0.033, so they explain most of that gap. Like for like (metal, with crew items) the group equations sit 0.033 above the metal fit. Stage 3's independent sizing (Anderson ch. 8) is the check.

Used outside its calibration (each carried with a band or flagged for Stage 3):

- Table 3.1 and Table 6.2 empty-weight fits and the GA group weights (15.46)-(15.57): crewed aircraft, used without crew items.
- Table 6.3 fuselage length: crewed aircraft; it sets the tail arm and the fuselage wetted area.
- Table 3.4 consumption (rubber, TP-R90 and PT6A-42 rows): large turboprops. The TP100 uses its datasheet cruise value also at loiter; its part-power value is unknown.
- Table 10.4 turboprop weight and size: 400-5,000 bhp; the rubber engine and the TP100 are below it.
- (13.9) power lapse: piston engines, applied to turboprops.
- (12.49) span efficiency: a straight-wing fit; it sets the optimum aspect ratio.
- Downwash: the far-wake value in place of Raymer's chart.
- Gear and tyre drag per area: DR-1's readings of Raymer's gear-drag table.

## 11. Risks, each with its Stage 3 measurement

| Risk | Effect if wrong | Stage 3 measurement |
|---|---|---|
| Turboprop power lapse (piston (13.9) used) | ceiling binds the engine; a better lapse leaves margin, a worse one fails R12 | Mattingly App. K off-design analysis at 20,000 and 25,000 ft |
| TP100 consumption at loiter part power (cruise value used) | about 0.51 throttle at loiter; fuel and W0 move directly | Mattingly App. K part-power SFC; the datasheet |
| Empty weight of a crewless aircraft from crewed statistics | W0 through the sizing growth factor | Anderson ch. 8 independent weight estimate |
| Section CL_max 1.5 (judgement) | sets the loiter and cruise speeds through the 1.3 V_stall floor and the stall limit | SU2 polar of the chosen section after a NACA-data validation row |
| Span efficiency (12.49) and downwash (far-wake value) | optimum aspect ratio; static margin and tail size | vortex lattice: span loading, e, downwash at the tail |
| Gear stowage (track wider than the fuselage, wing too thin) | sponsons or a wider belly add drag and weight not modelled | layout in preliminary design; drag of the chosen stowage by the build-up |
| Rotation without ground effect; assumed tail CL limits | tail size | lattice with a ground image; elevator sizing |
| TP100 data from search extracts | every engine number | read the datasheet before Gate B |

## 12. Open items for Gate A round 3

1. **Concept**: with the round-1 weights the pusher scores 4.13 against 3.95. Éder's round-2 answer (tractor) was given on figures that the rotation sign error had distorted, so it is asked again.
2. **Negative gust**: -2.09 at zero-fuel weight against -1.8.
3. **The 1.3 V_stall speed floor** (it sets the loiter speed) and **R16** (30 deg bank at loiter): not yet ruled.
4b. **V_C placard**: the structure is sized at the full-power maximum level speed (185 kt EAS), which sets q and the gust; the mission flies far slower.
4c. **Gear stowage**: neither concept can retract its wheels into the wing; sponsons or a wider belly are needed (not modelled).
4. **Engine data**: the PBS_TP100 figures are search extracts; the datasheet must be read before Gate B. Its part-power consumption at loiter is unknown (the cruise value is used).
5. The rotation and trim checks rest on two assumed tail lift limits (ledger).
